categories.name: Directional terms
categories.summary: Words that describe where one structure lies relative to another, always with the body in the anatomical position: standing, facing forward, palms forward.

categories.name: Planes & sections
categories.summary: The imaginary flat surfaces used to slice the body for description and imaging.

categories.name: Movements
categories.summary: The standard vocabulary for joint movement.

categories.name: Regions & cavities
categories.summary: Named areas and spaces of the body.

categories.name: Structural terms
categories.summary: Words that name kinds of anatomical parts.

categories.name: Word parts
categories.summary: Prefixes and suffixes that unlock most medical words.

categories.name: Disease processes
categories.summary: The handful of ways tissue goes wrong. Almost every diagnosis is one of these processes happening in a particular place.

categories.name: Clinical terms
categories.summary: The words clinicians use to describe how illness behaves, how it is found and where it is heading.

terms.definition: Toward the front of the body.
terms.example: The sternum is anterior to the heart.

terms.definition: Toward the back of the body.
terms.example: The vertebral column is posterior to the oesophagus.

terms.definition: Toward the belly side; in humans the same as anterior.
terms.example: The ventral root of a spinal nerve carries motor fibres.

terms.definition: Toward the back; in humans the same as posterior.
terms.example: The dorsal surface of the hand is the back of the hand.

terms.definition: Above; toward the head.
terms.example: The heart is superior to the diaphragm.

terms.definition: Below; toward the feet.
terms.example: The bladder is inferior to the kidneys.

terms.definition: Toward the skull.
terms.example: The cranial end of the spinal cord joins the brainstem.

terms.definition: Toward the tail end of the body.
terms.example: The caudal part of the spinal cord ends at the cauda equina.

terms.definition: Closer to the midline of the body.
terms.example: The big toe is on the medial side of the foot.

terms.definition: Farther from the midline.
terms.example: The fibula is lateral to the tibia.

terms.definition: Closer to the point of attachment of a limb, or to the origin of a tube.
terms.example: The elbow is proximal to the wrist.

terms.definition: Farther from the attachment of a limb, or along a tube away from its origin.
terms.example: The fingers are distal to the wrist.

atlas.structure: Distal phalanx of right middle finger

terms.definition: Closer to the surface of the body.
terms.example: The great saphenous vein is superficial; the femoral vein is deep.

terms.definition: Farther from the surface, toward the interior.
terms.example: The femur lies deep to the thigh muscles.

terms.definition: On the same side of the body.
terms.example: The right hand and right foot are ipsilateral.

terms.definition: On the opposite side of the body.
terms.example: The left motor cortex controls the contralateral (right) hand.

terms.definition: On both sides.
terms.example: The kidneys are bilateral organs.

terms.definition: On one side only.
terms.example: A unilateral headache affects one side of the head.

terms.definition: Relating to the palm of the hand.
terms.example: The palmar interossei adduct the fingers.

atlas.structure: Set of palmar interossei of right hand

terms.definition: Relating to the sole of the foot.
terms.example: Plantar flexion points the foot downward.

terms.definition: A vertical plane dividing the body into left and right parts; the midsagittal (median) plane passes exactly through the midline.
terms.plain: A slice from front to back.
terms.example: A sagittal MRI of the spine shows the vertebrae in profile.

terms.definition: A vertical plane dividing the body into front and back parts.
terms.plain: A slice from side to side.
terms.example: Coronal CT images show both kidneys in one frame.

terms.definition: A horizontal plane dividing the body into upper and lower parts.
terms.plain: A slice across, like cutting a loaf.
terms.example: Most CT scans are viewed as transverse slices.

terms.definition: A cut made at right angles to the long axis of a structure.
terms.example: A cross-section of the femur shows the thick cortex around the marrow cavity.

terms.definition: A cut made along the long axis of a structure.
Bending a joint so the angle between the bones decreases.
terms.example: Bending the elbow is flexion; the biceps brachii is a flexor.

atlas.structure: Long head of right biceps brachii

terms.definition: Straightening a joint so the angle increases.
terms.example: The triceps extends the elbow.

atlas.structure: Long head of right triceps brachii

terms.definition: Moving a limb away from the midline of the body.
terms.example: The deltoid abducts the arm.

terms.definition: Moving a limb toward the midline.
terms.example: The adductor muscles of the thigh pull the legs together.

terms.definition: Turning a bone around its long axis; medial (internal) rotation turns the front surface inward, lateral (external) rotation turns it outward.
terms.example: The rotator cuff muscles rotate the humerus.

terms.definition: Moving a limb in a cone shape, combining flexion, abduction, extension and adduction.
terms.plain: Drawing a circle with the limb.
terms.example: Circling the arm at the shoulder.

terms.definition: Turning the forearm so the palm faces backward or down; in the foot, rolling the sole outward.
terms.example: Pronator teres and pronator quadratus pronate the forearm.

terms.definition: Turning the forearm so the palm faces forward or up.
terms.plain: Palm up, as if holding soup.
terms.example: The biceps is the most powerful supinator.

terms.definition: Bending the ankle so the toes point up toward the shin.
terms.example: Tibialis anterior dorsiflexes the foot.

terms.definition: Bending the ankle so the toes point down.
terms.example: Gastrocnemius and soleus plantar flex the ankle through the Achilles tendon.

terms.definition: Turning the sole of the foot inward.
terms.example: Ankle sprains usually happen in forced inversion.

terms.definition: Turning the sole of the foot outward.
terms.example: The fibularis muscles evert the foot.

terms.definition: Bringing the thumb across the palm to touch the fingertips.
terms.example: Opponens pollicis performs opposition.

terms.definition: Lifting a part upward, such as shrugging the shoulders.
Lowering a part, such as dropping the shoulders or opening the jaw.
Moving a part forward, such as pushing the shoulder blade forward.
Moving a part backward, such as squaring the shoulders.
Relating to the head, neck and trunk (the body's central axis).
terms.example: The axial skeleton includes the skull, spine and rib cage.

terms.definition: Relating to the limbs and the girdles that attach them.
terms.example: The appendicular skeleton has 126 bones.

terms.definition: The chest: the part of the trunk between the neck and the diaphragm, enclosed by the rib cage.
The part of the trunk between the diaphragm and the pelvis, containing most of the digestive organs.
The basin-shaped lowest part of the trunk, bounded by the hip bones and sacrum.
terms.plain: The bowl at the base of the trunk.

terms.definition: The region between the thighs below the pelvic floor, containing the external genitalia and anus.
The central compartment of the chest between the two lungs, containing the heart, great vessels, trachea and oesophagus.
The space inside the skull that holds the brain.
Lying behind the peritoneum, against the back wall of the abdomen.
terms.example: The kidneys, pancreas and aorta are retroperitoneal.

terms.definition: The internal organs of the body cavities, especially the abdomen.
A vessel carrying blood away from the heart, usually oxygenated.
A vessel carrying blood back to the heart, usually deoxygenated.
The finest blood vessels, one cell thick, where oxygen and nutrients pass into the tissues.
A band of tough connective tissue joining bone to bone.
A cord of connective tissue joining muscle to bone.
A flat sheet of tendon attaching a muscle over a wide area.
Sheets of connective tissue that wrap muscles and organs and divide the limbs into compartments.
Firm, flexible tissue that caps the ends of bones, joins the ribs to the sternum and shapes the nose, ears and airway.
An opening in a bone through which vessels or nerves pass.
terms.example: The spinal cord leaves the skull through the foramen magnum of the occipital bone.

terms.definition: A projection from a bone, often for muscle attachment.
terms.example: The xiphoid process is the tip of the sternum.

terms.definition: A rounded knob at the end of a bone forming a joint.
terms.example: The femoral condyles form the knee with the tibia.

terms.definition: A groove, especially the furrows between the gyri of the brain.
A ridge of the folded cerebral cortex.
A network of nerves or vessels.
terms.example: The brachial plexus supplies the arm.

terms.definition: A cluster of nerve cell bodies outside the brain and spinal cord.
A ring of muscle that closes an opening.
The three membranes (dura, arachnoid and pia mater) covering the brain and spinal cord.
A double fold of peritoneum that suspends an organ and carries its vessels.
Above normal, excessive.
terms.example: Hypertension: high blood pressure.

terms.definition: Below normal, deficient; also beneath.
terms.example: Hypothyroidism: an underactive thyroid. Hypodermic: beneath the skin.

terms.definition: Around.
terms.example: Pericardium: the sac around the heart.

terms.definition: Within, inside.
terms.example: Endocardium: the inner lining of the heart.

terms.definition: Outside.
terms.example: Exocrine glands secrete through ducts to a surface.

terms.definition: Upon, above.
terms.example: Epidermis: the layer on top of the dermis. Epigastric: above the stomach.

terms.definition: Below, under.
terms.example: Subclavian: beneath the clavicle. Infraspinatus: below the spine of the scapula.

terms.definition: Above.
terms.example: Supraspinatus: above the spine of the scapula.

terms.definition: Between.
terms.example: Intercostal: between the ribs. Intervertebral: between vertebrae.

atlas.structure: Intervertebral disk of first lumbar vertebra

terms.definition: Within.
terms.example: Intravenous: within a vein. Intracranial: within the skull.

terms.definition: Across, through.
terms.example: Transverse colon: the colon crossing the abdomen.

terms.definition: Without, lack of.
terms.example: Anaemia: lack of blood (red cells). Apnoea: absence of breathing.

terms.definition: Difficult, painful, abnormal.
terms.example: Dysphagia: difficulty swallowing. Dyspnoea: difficult breathing.

terms.definition: Slow / fast.
terms.example: Bradycardia: slow heart rate. Tachycardia: fast heart rate.

terms.definition: Half.
terms.example: Hemiplegia: paralysis of one side of the body.

terms.definition: Many, much.
terms.example: Polyuria: passing large amounts of urine.

terms.definition: Heart.
terms.example: Cardiology, myocardium, pericardium.

terms.definition: Lung, air.
terms.example: Pulmonary artery; pneumonia.

terms.definition: Liver.
terms.example: Hepatitis: inflammation of the liver.

terms.definition: Kidney.
terms.example: Nephrology; renal artery.

terms.definition: Stomach.
terms.example: Gastritis; gastroenterology.

terms.definition: Intestine.
terms.example: Enteritis; gastroenteritis.

terms.definition: Colon, large intestine.
terms.example: Colonoscopy; colitis.

terms.definition: Nerve, nervous system.
terms.example: Neurology; neuropathy.

terms.definition: Brain.
terms.example: Encephalitis: inflammation of the brain.

terms.definition: Muscle.
terms.example: Myocardium: heart muscle. Myalgia: muscle pain.

terms.definition: Bone.
terms.example: Osteoporosis; osteoarthritis.

terms.definition: Joint.
terms.example: Arthritis; arthroscopy.

terms.definition: Cartilage.
terms.example: Chondromalacia: softening of cartilage.

terms.definition: Vessel.
terms.example: Angiography: imaging of vessels. Vasodilation.

terms.definition: Blood.
terms.example: Haematology; haemorrhage.

terms.definition: Skin.
terms.example: Dermatology; epidermis.

terms.definition: Eye.
terms.example: Ophthalmology; oculomotor nerve.

terms.definition: Ear.
terms.example: Otitis: ear infection.

terms.definition: Nose.
terms.example: Rhinitis; rhinoplasty.

terms.definition: Bladder, sac.
terms.example: Cystitis: bladder infection. Cholecystectomy: removal of the gallbladder.

terms.definition: Inflammation.
terms.example: Appendicitis, tonsillitis, arthritis.

terms.definition: Surgical removal.
terms.example: Appendectomy: removal of the appendix.

terms.definition: Cutting into.
terms.example: Tracheotomy: an opening cut into the trachea.

terms.definition: Creating an opening.
terms.example: Colostomy: an opening of the colon onto the abdominal wall.

terms.definition: Looking inside with an instrument.
terms.example: Colonoscopy, arthroscopy, bronchoscopy.

terms.definition: Pain.
terms.example: Neuralgia: nerve pain. Myalgia: muscle pain.

terms.definition: Tumour or swelling.
terms.example: Melanoma, lipoma, haematoma.

terms.definition: Disease.
terms.example: Neuropathy, cardiomyopathy.

terms.definition: Surgical repair or reshaping.
terms.example: Angioplasty widens a narrowed artery.

terms.definition: Enlargement.
terms.example: Cardiomegaly; hepatomegaly.

terms.definition: Condition of the blood.
terms.example: Anaemia, hyperglycaemia, septicaemia.

terms.definition: Recording or imaging / the record produced.
terms.example: Angiography produces an angiogram; electrocardiography produces an ECG.

terms.definition: The body's protective response to injury or infection: blood vessels dilate and leak, and white cells move into the tissue.
terms.plain: Red, hot, swollen, painful: the body fighting back.
terms.example: Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix; the suffix -itis always means inflammation.

terms.definition: Invasion and multiplication of microorganisms (bacteria, viruses, fungi, parasites) in body tissue, usually provoking inflammation.
terms.plain: Germs growing where they should not.
terms.example: Pneumonia is an infection of the lung; a urinary tract infection usually starts in the bladder.

terms.definition: Gradual deterioration of a tissue's structure and function, through wear, ageing or a slow disease process rather than injury or infection.
terms.example: Osteoarthritis is degeneration of joint cartilage; a degenerated intervertebral disc loses height and can bulge.

atlas.structure: Intervertebral disk of fifth lumbar vertebra

terms.definition: Death of cells or tissue within the living body, from loss of blood supply, toxins, infection or physical damage.
terms.example: In a heart attack, heart muscle beyond the blocked artery undergoes necrosis within hours.

terms.definition: An abnormal mass of tissue formed when cells multiply beyond normal control; may be benign or malignant.
terms.example: A lipoma is a benign tumour of fat cells; a carcinoma is a malignant tumour of lining cells.

terms.definition: Of a tumour: not cancerous; it grows locally, does not invade neighbouring tissue and does not spread to distant sites, though it can still cause harm by pressure.
terms.example: Most pituitary tumours are benign, but a large one can press on the optic chiasm and affect vision.

terms.definition: Of a tumour: cancerous; able to invade surrounding tissue and spread (metastasise) to other parts of the body.
terms.example: A malignant tumour of the colon can invade through the bowel wall and spread to the liver via the portal vein.

terms.definition: The spread of cancer cells from where they started to a distant site, via the bloodstream or lymphatic vessels, where they form a new (secondary) tumour.
terms.example: Lung cancer commonly metastasises to bone, brain, liver and the adrenal glands.

terms.definition: Inadequate blood supply to a tissue, so that it receives too little oxygen to meet its needs; reversible if flow is restored in time.
terms.example: Angina is chest pain from ischaemia of heart muscle during exertion, when a narrowed coronary artery cannot deliver enough blood.

atlas.structure: Circumflex branch of left coronary artery

terms.definition: Death of tissue (an infarct) caused by loss of its blood supply; the end result of ischaemia that lasts too long.
terms.plain: Tissue dying because its blood supply was cut off.
terms.example: A myocardial infarction is a heart attack; a cerebral infarction is an ischaemic stroke.

atlas.structure: Sphenoid part of left middle cerebral artery

terms.definition: Swelling caused by excess fluid collecting in the tissues, from leaky capillaries, raised venous pressure, low blood protein or blocked lymph drainage.
terms.example: Ankle oedema in heart failure comes from raised pressure in the veins; pulmonary oedema is fluid in the lungs.

terms.definition: Formation of a blood clot (thrombus) inside a blood vessel or the heart, blocking flow.
terms.plain: A clot forming where it should not.
terms.example: Deep vein thrombosis is a clot in the deep veins of the leg, typically the femoral or popliteal vein.

terms.definition: Blockage of a blood vessel by material (an embolus) that has travelled through the bloodstream from elsewhere: usually a clot fragment, sometimes fat, air or tumour.
terms.example: A pulmonary embolism is a clot from a leg vein that has travelled through the right heart and lodged in a pulmonary artery.

terms.definition: Abnormal narrowing of a passage, vessel or valve opening.
terms.example: Aortic stenosis is a narrowed aortic valve; spinal stenosis narrows the canal around the spinal cord.

terms.definition: Enlargement of a tissue or organ because its cells grow bigger (not more numerous), usually in response to increased workload.
terms.example: The left ventricle hypertrophies in long-standing high blood pressure; skeletal muscle hypertrophies with strength training.

terms.definition: Wasting or shrinkage of a tissue or organ from loss of cell size or number, through disuse, loss of nerve or blood supply, ageing or malnutrition.
terms.example: The quadriceps atrophies within weeks of a leg being immobilised in a cast; the hippocampus atrophies in Alzheimer disease.

terms.definition: Of sudden onset and short duration; often severe. Describes timing, not seriousness.
terms.example: Acute appendicitis develops over hours; an acute kidney injury is a sudden drop in function.

terms.definition: Persisting for a long time, usually more than three months, or recurring; often develops slowly.
terms.example: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and chronic kidney disease are lifelong conditions managed rather than cured.

terms.definition: Of unknown cause, arising spontaneously.
terms.example: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis scars the lungs without an identifiable trigger.

terms.definition: Present from birth, whether inherited or caused by something during development in the womb.
terms.example: A ventricular septal defect is a congenital hole between the two ventricles of the heart.

terms.definition: Developed after birth, through infection, injury, lifestyle, environment or another disease, rather than being present from birth.
terms.example: Most heart valve disease in older adults is acquired, through wear, rheumatic fever or infection.

terms.definition: An objective feature of disease that an examiner can see, feel, hear or measure.
terms.example: A fever, a heart murmur and a swollen ankle are signs.

terms.definition: A subjective feature of disease that the person experiences and reports, which cannot be directly observed by others.
terms.example: Pain, nausea, dizziness and fatigue are symptoms; the clinician cannot measure them, only ask.

terms.definition: A recognisable group of signs and symptoms that occur together and characterise a particular condition, even when its cause is unknown or varied.
terms.example: Carpal tunnel syndrome is the pattern of numbness and weakness produced by compression of the median nerve at the wrist.

terms.definition: The identification of the disease or condition responsible for a person's signs and symptoms, reached through history, examination and tests.
terms.example: A diagnosis of pneumonia rests on the history, crackles on listening to the chest, and a shadow on the X-ray.

terms.definition: The list of conditions that could explain a presentation, ranked by likelihood and danger, which guides which tests to do next.
terms.example: The differential diagnosis of chest pain includes heart attack, pulmonary embolism, aortic dissection, reflux and a pulled muscle.

terms.definition: The expected course and outcome of a disease: the likelihood of recovery, recurrence, disability or death, based on evidence from similar cases.
terms.plain: What is likely to happen next.
terms.example: The prognosis of a small skin cancer removed early is excellent; the prognosis of metastatic pancreatic cancer is poor.

terms.definition: A period during which the signs and symptoms of a disease lessen or disappear, either temporarily or permanently, without the disease necessarily being cured.
terms.example: Inflammatory bowel disease alternates between remission and flares; leukaemia in remission has no detectable cancer cells.

terms.definition: The return of a disease or its symptoms after a period of improvement or remission.
terms.example: A relapse of multiple sclerosis brings new neurological symptoms lasting more than 24 hours.

terms.definition: Treatment given to prevent a disease or complication rather than to treat one that is already present.
terms.example: Anticoagulant injections after hip surgery are prophylaxis against deep vein thrombosis; vaccination is prophylaxis against infection.

terms.definition: Care or treatment aimed at relieving symptoms and improving quality of life rather than curing the disease; not limited to the end of life.
terms.plain: Comfort and quality of life, not cure.
terms.example: Palliative radiotherapy shrinks a painful bone metastasis without aiming to eliminate the cancer.
